decision: inventoried HeyTaco features and 9 competitors plus open-source clones
why: know what to match and where the gaps are before planning
result: no mature OSS clone; gaps: no redemption approval, silent over-limit, 1-endpoint API

decision: currency configurable per workspace, domain never says taco
why: Pearson keeps the taco habit, other adopters pick their own

decision: approval and balances stay in the app, fulfillment goes out via API and webhooks
why: refund on reject has to happen together with the ledger write
balances work like money, ledger shape is hard to change, cutover replaces a daily tool

decision: ordered work riskiest first: HeyTaco export, spec, ledger architecture, harness, then features
why: the export and the ledger shape can break everything built on top

decision: walked every HeyTaco admin page for Pearson in the browser
why: check the real config instead of trusting docs and reviews
evidence: docs/plan.md section Pearson's live HeyTaco setup
result: rewards are cash vouchers in soles, cancelling deletes data, export still pending

decision: downloaded all HeyTaco exports into data/heytaco and kept them out of git
why: the data has personal emails and the repo will be open source

decision: checked balances: received plus bonuses minus redeemed equals redeemable, joined by Slack user ID
why: this is the migration baseline the importer must reproduce

decision: flagged the 5093 vs 6557 all-time total gap
why: a number we can't explain can hide a migration bug

decision: wrote the domain spec with 108 numbered rules S1-S108 and 5 open assumptions
why: every module and test traces back to one rule id

decision: user settled A1 to A4: group mentions as a setting, duplicate reaction counts once, edits recompute, stickers optional and off by default
why: stickers are barely used (41 of 4726) and the unlock formula is hard to explain

decision: explained 5093 vs 6557: HeyTaco's total counts only current users as givers
why: unexplained numbers can hide migration bugs

decision: started an architecture arena with 3 independent designers (fable low, opus low, session model)
why: the ledger model and module boundaries are hard to change later, so compare designs before committing

decision: picked candidate 3 as the architecture base: one gift row, no stored balances, one command_log
why: fewest concepts and every piece of state has one owner; the judge picked it on its own too (26 vs 23 vs 18)

decision: grafted G1-G10: effects table, claim-first idempotency, separate app package, uniform member locks, Postgres concurrency suite, import cutoff, ack after execute, reaction re-add, completeness check, integer money
why: each fixes a gap the judge or I found in the base
evidence: docs/architecture.md How this design was chosen

decision: judge vendor check could not run: only Claude models are configured
why: the arena wants a judge from another vendor

decision: verified the synthesized artifacts: core-types compiles under tsc strict, replay script from the repo reconciles with 0 diffs and re-import adds 0
why: check the real files, not the candidates' summaries

decision: modeled redemptions, collaborative rewards and quests in TLA+ and checked them with TLC
why: these flows have the most states and the easiest money mistakes
result: VERIFIED all rules hold: 6 redemption, 6 collab, 4 quest, no deadlocks
